summary: Step M3-S02 (ui, metadata-builder) built: the two Classic case-intake email templates, their EmailFolder, the sender-identity note and package.xml, plus the deploy-order note written on this resume pass. Owning agent invoked per its own AGENT.md under the three Step 6 clauses; it verified the seven pre-existing outputs byte-identical against skills/admin/email-templates-and-alerts/references/metadata-and-sender-identity.md and changed none of them. Both declared checkers exit 0 with zero repair passes, check-outputs ok, both envelopes validate. The substantive finding is not a build defect: the plan's own two records of the acknowledgement sender disagree (Q22 reads support@ as a live routing address, answers-key.md reads it as never the routing address), and the cited skills forbid an auto-response senderEmail that is itself an Email-to-Case intake. No artefact of this step sets a sender, so the divergence is recorded in sender-identity-note.md for a human at the M3 gate rather than resolved here.

Not HIGH for those two reasons alone. Not LOW: the step was in `next` at claim time, every required input resolved from the plan, check-outputs exited 0, both envelopes validate, and nothing was written outside artefacts/M3-S02/ except the two contract-mandated envelope and report pairs.

process_observations.observation: The running -> running re-claim behaved as contract § 4 describes: set-status appended a fresh run rather than overwriting the interrupted one, so plan.json now carries all three runs and the interruption is visible rather than erased.

Resuming by re-invoking the owning agent, rather than writing deploy-order.md directly, kept the authoring boundary intact. The coordinator's resume message asked this agent to write it; agents/build-step-runner/AGENT.md 'What This Agent Does NOT Do' forbids authoring metadata, and metadata-builder Step 7 owns that file. The owning agent then grounded two ordering claims this agent would have asserted flat.

Two cited-adjacent skills contradict their own prose in their own worked examples, and this step is where it surfaces. admin/assignment-rules/references/metadata-examples.md:131 states senderEmail 'must never be the Email-to-Case routing address', then writes <senderEmail>support@acme.example</senderEmail> at :145 and :156 - while admin/email-to-case-configuration/references/metadata-examples.md:48 puts that same literal in <emailAddress> of a routing address. Whichever reading a human picks for this build, one of those two worked examples wants correcting at the skill.

One quotation in sender-identity-note.md § 1 is mis-attributed. It gives the OrgWideEmailAddress row of admin/email-deliverability-strategy/references/metadata-examples.md § 'Where each control actually lives' as 'No metadata type - API/Data Loader/Setup only'; that Deployable? cell (:27) reads only 'No metadata type', and the longer string belongs to the EmailDomainKey row above it (:24). The substantive claim - OrgWideEmailAddress has no metadata type - is correct and separately grounded in the sender-identity reference. Reported, not repaired: an artefact is not this agent's to edit.

The plan holds two incompatible records of one decision and no artefact of this step can settle it. plan.json clarification Q22 (answered) says 'support@ (a live routing address) itself sends the acknowledgement'; answers-key.md's Acknowledgement row says 'from support@acme.example (an org-wide email address, never the Email-to-Case routing address itself)'. Both cited skills forbid an auto-response senderEmail that is an Email-to-Case intake address. EmailTemplate carries no sender element, so nothing here changes either way - the element that turns on it is M3-S04's senderEmail. Left to a human at the M3 gate, per the step's manual test B06.

The control the plan names against the loop is half inert as configured, and the owning agent marked rather than asserted it. 'Fires once per case' is grounded (Q63) but bounds fan-out per case, not a loop whose growth is one new case per round trip. 'The routing address rejects its own sender' depends on authorizedSenders, which email-to-case-configuration tells you to leave empty for a public support address - so unauthorizedSenderAction never fires. What actually stands between this build and the loop is the Q68 sandbox loop test, which is detection, and a mail-server setting outside Salesforce.

The concurrency constraint held. M3-S01 moved from running to built underneath this run (the other runner finished it); nothing in this run read-modify-wrote anything under artefacts/M3-S01/, and every checker was invoked at --manifest-dir artefacts/M3-S02 rather than at build scope, so a half-built sibling tree could not have entered this step's exit codes.

deploy-order.md is written on every metadata-builder run and is declared by no step in this build - not M1-S01, M1-S02, or any of the five M2 steps. Every such step therefore books a permanent undeclared artefact and cannot score HIGH under this agent's Step 9 rubric. The fix is one amend-step per pending step to add the path, not a change to either agent.
